_comment: Free-tier allowances per provider. These are UPPER BOUNDS taken from each provider's published limits on the date above; free tiers change constantly, so re-verify before relying on a figure. For a GitHub Copilot workload the binding limit is usually requests_per_minute or requests_per_day, NOT the headline token pool — Mistral is the clearest example, with ~1B tokens/month behind roughly 2 requests/minute. 'tos' records whether the provider's terms are comfortable with a self-hosted personal proxy: many free tiers restrict proxy or relay use, and that is a real cost of a free tier that belongs next to the quota rather than buried. Informational, not legal advice.

free_types.recurring-daily: Resets every day. Counted as daily_tokens x days-in-month for the monthly headline.
free_types.recurring-uncapped: Permanently free but no published token cap (rate/concurrency limited). Listed, never summed — extrapolating a rate limit to 24/7 produces a fantasy number.
free_types.one-time-credit: A signup credit that does not recur. Kept in a separate total so it never inflates the steady figure.
free_types.none: No free tier; the provider is pay-as-you-go.

providers.tos_note: The consumer terms scope API use to personal needs and restrict making keys available to third parties. Fine for a single-user proxy; read them if you share the instance.
providers.notes: Largest free token pool of any provider, but ~2 RPM makes it a fallback for chat rather than a primary for completions.

providers.tos_note: The services agreement prohibits reselling or redistributing API access. Personal single-user use is the ordinary reading.
providers.notes: Per-model daily token budgets; exhaustion arrives as a 429 naming the daily limit and its UTC reset.
Very fast inference; the 5 RPM ceiling is the practical limit, not the token budget.

providers.tos_note: The free tier is scoped to developers building with Google AI models.
providers.notes: The Flash family shares ONE pool — counting each variant separately is the mistake that inflates these numbers several-fold.

providers.tos_note: The self-serve terms restrict using the service to provide a proxy to others. A personal instance is the ordinary reading.
providers.notes: Budget is 10,000 neurons/day, not tokens: roughly 200-400 requests on a small model and far fewer on a large one. Resets at UTC midnight.

providers.tos_note: Prohibits building competing products; no explicit position on a self-hosted personal proxy.
Prohibits reselling API access or building a competing service.
providers.notes: Only :free-suffixed models. A one-time $10 lifetime top-up raises the free allowance from 50 to 1000 requests/day — reported separately because it is not a recurring grant.

providers.tos_note: The terms prohibit making the service available to third parties or reselling it.
providers.notes: No published token cap on the free models, so it is listed but never summed. 50 requests/day without purchased credit, ~1000/day with. The .cn platform requires a Chinese phone number.

providers.tos_note: The free tier is explicitly for prototyping, development, research and evaluation — not for serving real end users.
providers.notes: Rate-limited with no published token cap, so listed and not summed.
The GLM Flash models are permanently free with no published token cap.

providers.tos_note: The open platform terms permit broad use including derivative product development.
providers.notes: Signup credit only — it does not recur, so it is excluded from the steady monthly figure.
